| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | £41.2m | £35.2m | +17.0% | £118.3m | £119.0m |

- Revenue was £41.2m, up 17.0% on Q3 2025 and 4.3% on Q2 2026. It was £313k (0.8%) below the budget of £41.5m: Checkout and Payouts were slightly behind in July and August, and September beat budget once the two payroll bureaus went live on Payouts on 1 September.

- Gross margin was 58.0%, up 0.6 points on Q2 and 1.9 points on a year ago, and 0.5 points below budget. Fraud losses (£83k over budget) and hosting usage above our committed capacity (£36k over) explain most of the gap.

- EBITDA was £2.1m (5.2% of revenue) against a budget of £2.4m. Operating costs were £145k under budget: staff costs were £310k under because hiring is behind plan, and professional fees were £305k over.

- Headcount was 604 against a budget of 618. Following the exec decision of 11 September, non-critical backfills are paused from 1 October, and we now forecast 625 at year end against a budget of 640.

- Cash was £70.1m at 30 September (£71.3m at 30 June). This excludes customer funds, which are held in safeguarding accounts.

- Sales and marketing rose £180k on Q2 because of the September merchant acquisition campaign in Ireland, but stayed £40k under budget.

passages.text:
## 6. New suppliers and changes to bank details

Changes to bank details are the most common way fraudsters steal from finance teams. Treat every request as suspicious until it is verified.

- New suppliers are set up on form AP-03 with the company number, VAT number and bank details on the supplier's letterhead. AP checks the company at Companies House (or the national register) and screens it against the sanctions lists.

- Any change to bank details must be verified by phone. Call the supplier on a number we already hold, never on a number given in the request, and the call must be made by someone other than the person who received the request. Record who you spoke to, when, and on which number.

- Cooling-off: new details take effect two working days after verification.

- Confirmation of Payee: run it for every new or changed GBP account. If the name does not match, stop and escalate to Tom Whitfield.

- First payment to new details: if it is over £10,000, it needs Financial Controller approval even if the amount would otherwise fall in the AP Specialist's band.

- Email-only requests to change bank details are reported the same day to Tom Whitfield and to Lena Fischer (Security Engineer), with the original email attached.
passages.title: Supplier Payment Run Procedure.docx

passages.text:
## 7. Personal data breaches

7.1 Sorrel will notify Kestrel of any personal data breach without undue delay, and in any case within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, by email to privacy@kestrelpay.example and by phone to Kestrel's security on-call number.

7.2 Within 72 hours Sorrel will send what it knows of the nature of the breach, the data and people affected, the likely consequences and the steps taken.

7.3 Kestrel decides whether to notify the Information Commissioner's Office and the people affected. Sorrel will not notify anyone about a breach of Kestrel data without Kestrel's agreement, unless the law requires it.

# Management accounts: August 2026

Kestrel Pay Ltd and Kestrel Pay Europe Ltd, combined, in GBP. Unaudited. Issued on WD8, Thursday 10 September 2026, by Tom Whitfield (Financial Controller) with Jonas Berg (FP&A Manager). Reviewed by Daniel Reyes (CFO).

## 1. Summary

Table 1: Income summary, £000

| Line | August 2026 | August budget | Variance | July 2026 | Q3 to date | Q3 to date budget |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | 13,401 | 13,650 | (249) | 13,520 | 26,921 | 27,350 |
| Gross profit | 7,746 | 7,990 | (244) | 7,815 | 15,561 | 16,000 |
| Gross margin | 57.8% | 58.5% | (0.7) pts | 57.8% | 57.8% | 58.5% |
| Operating costs | (7,156) | (7,230) | 74 | (7,114) | (14,270) | (14,460) |
| EBITDA | 590 | 760 | (170) | 701 | 1,291 | 1,540 |

- Revenue was £249k (1.8%) below budget. UK card volume fell more than usual in August: Checkout payment volume was £1.58bn against £1.66bn in July. The 47-minute Checkout outage on 17 August (INC-2026-0817) cost about £7,900 of revenue, and the service credits to Checkout Pro merchants (about £2,650) are netted off August revenue. Payouts was flat on July; the two payroll bureaus went live on 1 September.

- Gross margin was 57.8%. Two merchant fraud cases added £61k of losses, of which £12k has been recovered so far.

- Operating costs were £74k under budget. Staff costs were under because headcount is 597 against a budget of 611; professional fees were over, mainly Carrow Finch's fees on the Dublin office lease (£85k).

- Year to date (January to August) revenue is £104.0m against a budget of £104.9m.

## 2. Revenue by product

| Kestrel Accounts | 3,402 | 3,398 | 2,951 | +15.3% |
| Kestrel Payouts | 2,701 | 2,691 | 2,160 | +25.0% |
| Total | 13,401 | 13,520 | 11,531 | +16.2% |

## 3. Key measures at 31 August 2026

| Measure | 31 August 2026 | 31 July 2026 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Merchant customers | 49,310 | 48,790 |
| Checkout payment volume in the month | £1.58bn | £1.66bn |
| Payouts volume in the month | £0.63bn | £0.64bn |
| Business accounts open | 31,050 | 30,820 |
| Customer funds safeguarded | £1.26bn | £1.25bn |
| Headcount | 597 | 593 |
| Kestrel's own cash | £70.8m | £71.0m |

## 4. Cash

Cash fell by £0.2m in August, to £70.8m. EBITDA of £0.6m was more than used by capital spending of £0.9m (mostly capitalised development) and lease payments of £0.2m, with net interest of £0.1m received and a £0.2m inflow from working capital. Customer funds in the safeguarding accounts are not included.

## 5. Points for the exec team

| 1. | Q3 timetable. The preliminary Q3 2026 Quarterly Report comes out on 30 September, before the close. Flash revenue for September goes to the exec team on WD3, Monday 5 October. |
| --- | --- |
| 2. | Payouts bureaus. Both bureaus went live on 1 September as planned. Together they should add about £0.2m of Payouts revenue a month. |
| 3. | Brindle Print & Post. The print contract (KPC-2025-0204) expires on 30 September. Hannah Kim needs to agree the renewal, or we will be invoiced at Brindle's proposed new rate of £1.62 a pack against our current £1.58. |
| 4. | Hosting usage. Ashgrove usage was within the committed capacity in August, but September Payouts volumes may take it over. Nadia Kowalski is watching it. |
| 5. | Safeguarding audit. Fernside & Co started interim fieldwork for the 2026 safeguarding audit on 7 September; the £140k fee will fall in September instead of Q4. |

Brackets show costs, losses and adverse variances. There was no tax charge in Q3 2025 because of losses brought forward.

Commentary on the income statement

- Cost of revenue was £79k over budget. Fraud losses and chargebacks were £83k over, mostly two merchant fraud cases in August (£61k, of which £12k has been recovered so far). Processing and hosting was £36k over because Payouts traffic in September pushed usage above the committed capacity in our hosting contract with Ashgrove Cloud Services (KPC-2026-0142). Interchange and scheme fees were £60k under, in line with lower Checkout volume.

- Staff costs were £310k under budget. Average headcount in the quarter was 597 against a budgeted 608.

- Professional fees were £305k over budget, for three reasons: interim fieldwork for the 2026 safeguarding audit by Fernside & Co LLP (£140k, KPC-2026-0326), brought forward from Q4; legal fees for the Dublin office lease (£85k); and EU VAT and OSS registration advice from Ostrander Tax Advisers LLP (£80k, KPC-2026-0301).

- Sales and marketing rose £180k on Q2 because of the September merchant acquisition campaign in Ireland, but stayed £40k under budget.

- Net finance income is interest on Kestrel's own cash. It does not include any return on customer funds.
